newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - European debt vols slide as bonds firm.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - European debt vols slide as bonds firm.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options slid on Friday after bond markets firmed following U.S. growth data, brokers said on Friday. They said the volatility decline was widespread, with Euromarks also suffering.
Implied volatility of March Bund options on March futures slid to 5.60 percent from 5.73 percent at the open, and traders said it was likely to continue to slide.

"Once the figures came out, volatility went back down to about 5.6 - 5.7 percent which is around the support level," said Luke White, a broker at Fimat Futures UK, adding that it was a fair value just before the weekend.
March Bund volatility has been mired around the 5.7 percent mark ahead of the GDP figures which showed a rise of 4.7 percent against expectations of 3.9 percent growth.
"Volatility wanted to go lower, and the Bund rally gave it the chance," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London.
"It's heading for a close around 5.5 percent," he said.
Traders said time decay was also likely to hit the options over the weekend.
March Bund futures were up 0.48 at 101.70 by 1615 GMT.
"On the whole, volatility has drifted off across all the markets, short and long term," White said.
He said Euromarks volatility had been sold less than Pibor vols but was suffering nonetheless.
In the Italian market, BTP puts were popular, dealers said. They noted decent volumes in 128.00-130.00 put spreads.
March BTP futures were last up 10 basis points at 130.57.
